page: Amazon Web Services i3en.3xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It features 12 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz, with 6 physical cores and hyper-threading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a resource-dense 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. A key hardware highlight is the inclusion of 7500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core processing, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the lower 25th percentile, indicating weaker single-threaded performance. However, multi-core CPU execution and memory bandwidth tests consistently achieve average tier results. The system demonstrates solid throughput for data-heavy operations, with static web serving reaching 9.21 GB/sec and Redis SET operations executing at 9.96 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers high value for workloads requiring massive local storage capacity and high memory density without the premium of dedicated high-compute processors. The trade-off lies in its modest single-core CPU performance and limited suitability for complex machine learning tasks, as shown by poor medium-model LLM inference speeds. It is highly suited for NoSQL databases, distributed file systems, transactional databases, and data warehousing workloads that rely heavily on fast local NVMe storage and high memory capacity.
description: Amazon Web Services i3en.3xlarge is a storage-optimized instance designed for data-intensive workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 12 vCPUs and 6 physical cores, it features 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory and a substantial 7500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 12 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results show average multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth, though single-core performance is relatively weak. This hardware profile makes the instance highly cost-efficient for storage-heavy and memory-intensive applications rather than compute-bound tasks. It is well-suited for distributed databases, transactional systems, and large-scale data warehousing.
